Builds and validates a program cache record from ELF data, or initializes a nonexecutable record.

# Purpose
`fd_progcache_rec.c` builds and initializes a program cache record for an SBPF program. The main function, [`fd_progcache_rec_new`](<#fd_progcache_rec_new>), takes ELF metadata, loader configuration, feature flags, program bytes, and scratch memory, then lays out a `fd_progcache_rec_t` object in caller supplied memory. It also allocates space for call destination data and read only data, stores offsets and sizes in the record, and prepares an `fd_sbpf_program_t` view so the SBPF loader can write the loaded program into the record-backed memory.

After the loader step, the code creates a syscall table for the given `load_slot`, loads the ELF image with `fd_sbpf_program_load`, and then creates and initializes a `fd_vm_t` instance to validate the loaded bytecode with `fd_vm_validate`. If loading or validation fails, the function returns `NULL`. On success, it marks the record as executable, stores the load slot and entry point, and returns the initialized record. The file also defines [`fd_progcache_rec_new_nx`](<#fd_progcache_rec_new_nx>), which creates a non-executable record by clearing the object and storing only the slot value.
